'''Lawrence David Guth''' ({{IPAc-en|g|uː|θ}}; born 1977) is a professor of mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name=profile>{{cite web|url=https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.html?pid=1461|title=Larry Guth|work=Directory|publisher=MIT Mathematics|access-date=2025-05-10}}</ref>

==Education and career==

Guth graduated from [[Yale University]] in 2000 with a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] in mathematics.<ref name="MIT_CV">{{Cite web | url= https://math.mit.edu/documents/uploads/cv/2015_04_14_CV_lguth.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae Larry Guth |publisher=MIT Mathematics Department |quote=B.S. Mathematics, Yale University, 2000 |date=2020 |access-date=February 20, 2020}}</ref>

In 2005, he received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), where he studied geometry of objects with random shapes under the supervision of [[Tomasz Mrowka]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy |name=Lawrence Guth|id=34061}}.</ref><ref name="Father"/>

After MIT, Guth went to [[Stanford]] as a postdoc and later to the [[University of Toronto]] as an assistant professor on a tenure track.<ref name="NYU2011"/>

In 2011, [[New York University]]'s [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] hired Guth as a professor, listing his areas of interest as "[[metric geometry]], [[harmonic analysis]], and [[geometric combinatorics]]."<ref name="NYU2011">{{Cite web |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/newsletters/Fall2011.pdf |title=New Faculty: Larry Guth  |publisher=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at NYU |quote= He was a postdoc at Stanford and an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto. He received a Sloan fellowship in 2010. |date=2011 |access-date=February 20, 2020}}</ref>

In 2012, Guth moved to MIT, where he is Claude Shannon Professor of Mathematics.<ref name=profile/>

==Research==
In his research, Guth has strengthened [[Gromov's systolic inequality for essential manifolds]]<ref>[https://mathandlife.blogspot.com/2009/07/guths-approach-to-gromovs-systolic.html Guth's approach to Gromov's systolic inequality], [[Shmuel Weinberger]], July 18, 2009.</ref> and, along with [[Nets Katz]], found a solution to the [[Erdős distinct distances problem]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/?pa=mathNews&sa=view&newsId=1062|series=Math In The News|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|title="Distinct Distance Problem in the Plane" Solved|date=March 2, 2011|access-date=May 27, 2011|archive-date=March 23, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323021425/http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/?pa=mathNews&sa=view&newsId=1062|url-status=dead}}.</ref> His interests include the [[Kakeya conjecture]] and the systolic inequality.

==Doctoral students==

Guth has supervised graduate students at the [[University of Toronto]] and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. His other doctoral students have included Dominic Dotterrer, Hannah Alpert, Ben Yang, Thao Do, Aleksandr Berdnikov, Alexey Balitskiy, Sahana Vasudevan, Yuqiu Fu, Shengwen Gan, Lingxian Zhang, and Sarah Tammen.<ref name="GuthCV">{{cite web
 |url=https://math.mit.edu/documents/uploads/cv/2024_08_26_CV_larryg.pdf
 |title=Curriculum Vitae: Larry Guth
 |publisher=MIT Mathematics
 |date=August 26, 2024
 |format=PDF
 |access-date=July 31, 2026
}}</ref> His doctoral student [[Hong Wang (mathematician)|Hong Wang]] received her PhD from MIT in 2019 under his supervision and was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 2026 for her work in [[harmonic analysis]] and [[geometric measure theory]].<ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-alumni-awarded-fields-medal-0728
 |title=Yu Deng '11 and Hong Wang PhD '19 awarded Fields Medal
 |last=Kwok
 |first=Natalie
 |publisher=MIT News
 |date=July 28, 2026
 |access-date=July 31, 2026
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2026
 |title=Fields Medals 2026
 |publisher=International Mathematical Union
 |access-date=July 31, 2026
}}</ref>

==Recognition==

Guth won an Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.artsci.utoronto.ca/main/newsitems/five-u-of-t-scientists-awarded-prestigious-sloan-fellowships |title=February 19, 2010 — Five U of T scientists awarded prestigious Sloan Fellowships — Faculty of Arts & Science |access-date=October 23, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616122908/http://www.artsci.utoronto.ca/main/newsitems/five-u-of-t-scientists-awarded-prestigious-sloan-fellowships |archive-date=June 16, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was an invited speaker at the [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|International Congress of Mathematicians]] in India in 2010, where he spoke about [[systolic geometry]].<ref>[http://www.math.toronto.edu/cms/assets/MathFiles/Alumni/In-The-News/Newsletters/Files/Newsletter2010.pdf Fall newsletter 2010], Univ. of Toronto mathematics department, retrieved May 26, 2011.</ref><ref>[http://www.icm2010.org.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers ICM listing of invited speakers] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717191917/http://www.icm2010.org.in/scientific-program/invited-speakers |date=July 17, 2011 }}, retrieved May 26, 2011.</ref>

In 2013, the [[American Mathematical Society]] awarded Guth its annual [[Salem Prize]], citing his "major contributions to geometry and combinatorics."<ref name="AMS_Salem">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201403/rnoti-p296.pdf |title=Guth Awarded 2013 Salem Prize |work=Notices of the AMS |quote=Lawrence Guth of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology has been awarded the 2013 Salem Prize for his "major contributions to geometry and combinatorics. His brilliant insights led to the solution of old problems and the introduction of powerful new techniques," according to the prize citation. |date=2014 |access-date=February 20, 2020}}</ref>

In 2014 he received a [[Simons Investigator Award]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-and-physical-science/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees |title= Simons Investigator Awardees |publisher= Simons Foundation |access-date= September 11, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170806190912/https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-and-physical-science/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees/ |archive-date= August 6, 2017 |url-status= dead }}</ref>
In 2015, he received the [[Clay Research Award]].<ref>[http://www.claymath.org/events/news/2015-clay-research-award Clay Research Award 2015]</ref>

He was included in the 2019 class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to harmonic analysis, combinatorics and geometry, and for exposition of high level mathematics".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2019 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=November 7, 2018}}</ref>

On February 20, 2020, the [[National Academy of Sciences]] announced that Guth is the first winner of their new $20,000 [[Maryam Mirzakhani]] Prize in Mathematics for mid-career mathematicians. The citation states that his award is "for developing surprising, original, and deep connections between geometry, analysis, topology, and combinatorics, which have led to the solution of, or major advances on, many outstanding problems in these fields."<ref>{{cite tweet |author-link= |user=theNASciences |number=1230508007538266112 |date= February 20, 2020|title= The inaugural recipient for the Maryam Mirzakhani Prize in Mathematics, Larry Guth of @MIT|script-title= |trans-title= |language= |retweet= |link= https://twitter.com/theNASciences/status/1230508007538266112|access-date= February 20, 2020}}</ref><ref name="2020NASonline">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2020-awards/Guth.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200124083217/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2020-awards/Guth.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 24, 2020 |title=2020 Maryam Mirzakhani Prize in Mathematics |publisher=NAS |quote=Guth is receiving the $20,000 prize 'for developing surprising, original, and deep connections between geometry, analysis, topology, and combinatorics, which have led to the solution of, or major advances on, many outstanding problems in these fields.' The Mirzakhani prize honors exceptional contributions to the mathematical sciences by a mid-career mathematician |date=February 20, 2020 |access-date=February 20, 2020}}</ref> He was one of three recipients of the 2020 [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]].<ref name=Bocher2020>{{cite journal|title=2020 Bôcher Memorial Prize|date=April 2020 |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202004/rnoti-p546.pdf |volume=67|issue=4|pages=546–549}}.</ref> In 2021, he was elected member of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]]<!--, where he may meet with his father-->.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426172730/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 26, 2021|title=News from the National Academy of Sciences|date=April 26, 2021|access-date=July 2, 2021|quote=Newly elected members and their affiliations at the time of election are:  ...  Guth, Larry; Claude Shannon Professor, department of mathematics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge}}</ref>

==Personal==
He is the son of [[Alan Guth]], a [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] known for the theory of [[Inflation (cosmology)|inflation]] in cosmology.<ref name="Father">{{Cite web |url=https://news.mit.edu/2014/profile-larry-guth-0527 |title=Like father, like son |last=Knight |first=Helen |publisher=MIT News |quote=Guth moved to MIT as a graduate student, where he began studying geometry under the supervision of mathematics professor Tomasz Mrwoka. |date=May 27, 2014 |access-date=February 20, 2020}}</ref>
